driving_reasons_vocabulary.curiosityDriven: pursued mainly to explore, learn or understand something for its own sake — the pull is 'I want to find out'.
driving_reasons_vocabulary.individualInternalProblems: driven by resolving one's own inner struggles, growth wounds or personal demons through the work.
driving_reasons_vocabulary.interpersonalInternalProblems: driven by fixing or navigating relationships and emotional dynamics between people.
driving_reasons_vocabulary.externalProblems: driven by solving concrete real-world problems out in the world — technical, social, environmental, systemic.
driving_reasons_vocabulary.personalGrowth: pursued to build oneself — mastery, discipline, becoming more capable over time.
driving_reasons_vocabulary.socialRecognition: driven by status, being seen, respected, admired or validated by others.
driving_reasons_vocabulary.effortlessEngagement: pursued because it produces flow with little friction — the work draws on factors the student is naturally strong in, so it feels easy and natural rather than effortful. Low resistance plus high absorption; not external reward, not problem-solving, but FIT between innate strengths and what the work demands.

known_limitation: The three samples come from ONE model scoring the same rubric three times, not from three independent raters. Correlated error is likely and sample_variance therefore UNDERSTATES true uncertainty — a factor all three passes agree on may still be wrong together. Treat low variance as 'the rubric was unambiguous', never as 'this is correct'. Every record starts review_status: unreviewed for that reason.
